questions.question: Who developed the theory of cultural dimensions based on a large study of IBM employees?
questions.explanation: Dutch social psychologist Geert Hofstede identified cultural dimensions such as individualism/collectivism and power distance from research across over 70 countries.

questions.question: What characterizes high-context communication, according to Edward T. Hall?
options: Much of the meaning is implicit and carried by context, relationships, and non-verbal cues
Everything is stated directly and explicitly
Communication happens only in formal meetings
questions.explanation: In high-context cultures (e.g., Japan), meaning relies heavily on shared context and indirect signals; low-context cultures (e.g., Germany, USA) favour explicit messages.

questions.question: What does Hofstede's "power distance" dimension describe?
options: How a culture accepts and expects unequal distribution of power
How far a country is from the equator
questions.explanation: Power distance measures how much hierarchy and unequal power are accepted - affecting, for example, how employees address their bosses.

questions.question: In which book did Edward T. Hall introduce high- and low-context communication?
questions.explanation: The American anthropologist Edward T. Hall introduced the high-context/low-context distinction in his 1976 book "Beyond Culture".

questions.question: Why is intercultural competence important when using English internationally?
options: Shared language does not guarantee shared cultural norms, so misunderstandings can still occur
Grammar is all that matters in communication
Culture is identical everywhere English is spoken
It guarantees you will never make mistakes
questions.explanation: Even with English as a common language, differences in directness, politeness, and non-verbal norms can cause misunderstanding - cultural awareness matters.
